_what: The words of each email the sign-in sends, by the kind auth.mjs gives (otp-<type> for an email code, by Better Auth's emailOTP types; the link kinds by their callback). Each {field} is the message's own value: otp, url, newEmail, and minutes (settings.json email_code, the same minutes the pages say). send-email.mjs fills them; the provider gets them as subject, text and html. `text` is the plain part; the html says `markdown` (else `text`), drawn in email-look.json, with an `action` button ({label, href}) under it where the message is a link. Where the plain part holds a link, `markdown` leaves it to the button.

otp-sign-in.subject: Your {name} sign-in code: {otp}
text: Your code to sign in to {name} is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask to sign in, you can ignore this email.

otp-email-verification.subject: Your {name} code: {otp}
text: Your code to prove this address for {name} is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

otp-forget-password.subject: Your {name} password code: {otp}
text: Your code to set a new {name} password is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, your password stays as it is.

otp-change-email.subject: Your {name} code: {otp}
text: Your code to change your {name} address is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

magic-link.subject: Sign in to {name}
text: Open this link to sign in to {name}:
{url}
If you did not ask to sign in, you can ignore this email.

If you did not ask to sign in, you can ignore this email.
